Gold.note: Central bank buying and macro hedging demand sustain momentum despite elevated levels.

Silver.note: Industrial solar demand combined with precious metal monetary premium drives upside.

Copper.note: Tight concentrate markets and robust electrification demand offset broader macro headwinds.

Uranium.note: Structural supply deficits and renewed global nuclear build-out support long-term contract pricing.

Lithium.note: Near-term oversupply from new Australian and South American projects weighs on pricing.

Nickel.note: Surging Indonesian supply growth continues to outpace sluggish EV battery demand.

Zinc.note: Mine closures and tight treatment charges support prices despite modest demand growth.

Iron Ore.note: Weak Chinese property sector and high port inventories cap upside potential.

Coal.note: Ample global seaborne supply and long-term energy transition pressures limit price appreciation.

Rare Earths.note: Geopolitical export controls create premiums but near-term industrial demand remains soft.

Manganese.note: Steady global steel production balances against adequate South African supply.

PGM.note: Weak overall auto production offsets the structural substitution of platinum for palladium.

Potash.note: Normalizing global fertilizer inventories and adequate Eastern European supply ease pricing power.

Aluminum.note: Smelter curtailments in China and tight alumina supply constrain primary metal output.

Diversified.note: Broad exposure to base and precious metals provides balanced upside with manageable downside risk.
